title: Structural Characterization of the ASPSCR1-TFE3 Fusion Oncoprotein
content: Alveolar Soft Part Sarcoma (ASPS) is a rare and aggressive form of soft tissue sarcoma primarily affecting adolescents and young adults [1]. ASPS is caused by the t(X;17) chromosomal translocation that generates the ASPSCR1::TFE3 fusion gene [2, 3]. The ASPSCR1::TFE3 (AT3) fusion oncoprotein drives tumor progression by upregulating genes that are associated with angiogenesis and tumor metastasis [4, 5]. ASPS is also known for its poor prognosis and resistance to conventional therapies due to high metastatic potential [6, 7]. A recent study identified that Valosin Containing Protein (VCP, also known as p97) is a key co-factor of oncogenic AT3 [3]. VCP is an AAA+ type unfoldase involved in cellular processes including protein homeostasis, membrane fusion, and driving autophagic clearance of damaged organelles [8, 9]. Immunoprecipitation (IP) and immunofluorescence studies confirmed AT3 interaction with VCP in the nucleus of ASPS tumor cells from mouse, human cell lines, and human tumor samples [3]. Focusing on the structural basis of AT3-VCP interaction, our research aims to provide a foundation for developing VCP-targeted therapies to treat ASPS.
